findings.title: Failed work items are marked complete and their offsets are committed
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker catches every exception from result_processor, logs it, and then unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset() in the finally block. The commit loop can therefore commit past a message whose processing failed, so it will never be retried or sent to a DLQ. This directly contradicts the strategy docstring claiming it only commits offsets after successful processing and can silently lose uptime results.

findings.title: Unbounded queues provide no backpressure despite the documented guarantee
findings.body: FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit() never blocks or raises MessageRejected when workers fall behind. Arroyo will keep submitting messages as fast as Kafka delivers them, accumulating decoded WorkItems (including the original Kafka message) in memory indefinitely, growing OffsetTracker sets for uncommittable partitions as well. A slow subscription or downstream outage therefore risks OOM and massive reprocessing on restart rather than natural backpressure as claimed in the class docstring.

findings.title: Shared queue pool is destroyed by the first strategy close and reused after rebalance
findings.body: The FixedQueuePool (and its worker threads and OffsetTracker) is created once on the factory and handed to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy created by create_with_partitions(). Arroyo creates/closes strategies on partition assignment and rebalance; SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()/terminate() shuts down that shared pool, and queue.Queue.put() on a shut-down queue raises ShutDown. The next assignment reuses the same dead pool (factory only nulls it in factory.shutdown(), not on strategy close), so subsequent messages fail to enqueue, are swallowed by submit()'s broad except handler, and are marked complete without processing. The shared OffsetTracker also retains last_committed across assignments, so a partition reassigned at a lower offset can never be committed again.

findings.title: Close stops committing before queued work is drained
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() sets shutdown_event and joins the commit thread before shutting down the pool, and it never waits for queues to empty. FixedQueuePool.shutdown() sets worker.shutdown=True before calling queue.shutdown(immediate=False), so a worker that finishes its current item exits at the loop condition instead of draining remaining queued items. Consequently queued items are abandoned on graceful shutdown and any items workers do finish after the commit thread stops never have their offsets committed, causing avoidable duplicate reprocessing and violating the graceful-shutdown expectation.

findings.title: Group-to-queue assignment uses Python's randomized hash()
findings.body: get_queue_for_group() uses the built-in hash() on a string group key. For strings, hash() is randomized per interpreter process via PYTHONHASHSEED, so the same subscription maps to different queues in different processes and across restarts. That breaks the documented consistent-assignment/ordering guarantee whenever work for a group moves between consumer processes or the consumer restarts, and makes distribution non-reproducible; a stable digest (e.g. hashlib/md5, as used elsewhere in the uptime consumer) should be used instead.

findings.title: Submit swallows grouping/decoder failures and marks the offset complete
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit() wraps decoding, grouping and enqueueing in one broad except that logs the error and then add_offset()+complete_offset()s the message. Any failure in grouping_fn (or an enqueue failure such as a shut-down queue) therefore makes the message eligible for offset commit even though it was never processed, silently dropping it instead of surfacing the failure to Arroyo for retry/DLQ handling.
